one_liner: Rust/PyO3 memoization decorator for Python with SIEVE eviction, TTL, async and mmap cross-process backend; ~25x cachetools, slower than lru_cache.
what_it_does: A Python caching decorator, `@cache(max_size=128, ttl=None, backend="memory"|"shared")`, implemented as a Rust extension (PyO3/maturin). It wraps sync and async functions and returns a callable with `cache_info()` and `cache_clear()`. The memory backend keeps Python objects in-process. The shared backend serializes keys and values (a fast path for primitives, with a pickle fallback) into mmap'd files, so worker processes on one host share entries. For module-level functions it is a one-line swap for `functools.lru_cache` or `cachetools.func.lru_cache`, but there is no cache-object API.
how_it_is_fast: The whole hit path runs inside one PyO3 `tp_call`. It hashes the args tuple with `PyObject_Hash` and picks a shard with `hash & mask`. It probes a hashbrown table through a passthrough hasher that reuses Python's hash, using a borrowed-key `Equivalent` lookup so a hit allocates no key. It compares keys with `PyObject_RichCompareBool` and returns the value. On GIL builds the per-shard lock is `GilCell`, an `UnsafeCell` wrapper that does no locking because the GIL already serializes access; free-threaded builds compile in a parking_lot `RwLock` per shard instead. SIEVE eviction (NSDI'24) reduces a hit to one relaxed atomic store of a visited bit, with no LRU list relinking. The release build uses fat LTO and codegen-units=1. Most of the gap to cachetools is simply native code against a pure-Python wrapper plus a Condition lock.
when_to_use: Hot memoized functions called from thread pools or web-server threads on standard GIL CPython when you also want TTL or async in the same decorator. The author measured ~20M calls/s at 256 entries, against 0.8M for cachetools.func.lru_cache.

Replacing cachetools.func.lru_cache or ttl_cache decorators on hot paths. The author measured 19-27x more calls/s at 32-1024 entries, and 12-14x more than cachetools ttl_cache in the TTL loop (7.2-7.4M vs 0.52-0.60M).
Async functions. A cache hit returns without awaiting the coroutine, and concurrent misses on the same key are coalesced within each event loop.

Gunicorn or Celery workers on Linux or macOS that should share small results through mmap: keys up to 512 B and values up to 4 KB by default, primitives preferred. The author measured 5.0M ops/s in one process and 8.1M total with 4 processes.
Skewed or scan-heavy key streams where hit ratio matters more than call overhead. The author's Zipf tests show SIEVE with 15-22% fewer misses than LRU at the same size.
when_not_to_use: Plain memoization where you would otherwise use functools.lru_cache. The stdlib C cache is 1.3-1.8x faster single-threaded (31.0M vs 20.4M ops/s at 256 entries), and the CPython docs say it is already thread-safe (coherent under concurrent updates), so the repo's 'lru_cache + Lock' comparison adds a lock you do not need.

Free-threaded CPython. PyPI 0.7.0 ships no cp313t or cp314t wheels. The only published no-GIL results are from February 2026, before the current sharded store, and show total throughput falling from 15.1M ops/s at 1 thread to 3.0-4.2M at 8-32 threads. There is no newer data.

Code that needs features warp_cache lacks. Instance methods do not bind (open issue #52). There is no unbounded mode (max_size must be an int), no `typed=` flag, no custom key function, no dict-like cache object, no per-entry TTL, no stampede protection on sync calls, and no size-in-bytes eviction (#15 open). cachetools, cachebox or moka-py cover these.

Shared backend where a process can be SIGKILLed or OOM-killed mid-write. The cross-process TTAS spinlock has no owner-death recovery (#38 open), so every process hangs until the shm file is deleted. The shared backend is also unavailable on Windows and unsafe across trust boundaries, because complex types round-trip through pickle (#46, #50 open).

Production code that needs a stable release. The project has 9 stars and a Beta classifier, and the June 2026 memory-safety and concurrency fixes (#30, #31, #37, #39, #40) are on master but not in any PyPI release.

integration.dependencies: No Python runtime dependencies. Rust crates: pyo3 0.29, parking_lot 0.12 and hashbrown 0.15, plus memmap2, libc and ahash on non-Windows. Source builds need a Rust toolchain and maturin.
integration.min_toolchain: CPython 3.10+ on master (PyPI 0.7.0 declares >=3.9); Rust edition 2021, minimum rustc not documented
integration.platforms: PyPI 0.7.0 wheels: manylinux2014 x86_64/aarch64, macOS x86_64/arm64 and Windows x86_64 for CPython 3.9-3.14. No musllinux and no free-threaded wheels. The shared backend is POSIX-only and raises RuntimeError on Windows.
integration.thread_safety: The memory backend is safe to call from many threads without extra locking. On GIL builds it relies on the GIL (GilCell); free-threaded builds use a per-shard parking_lot RwLock. Concurrent sync misses on one key may each run the function; the async wrapper coalesces misses per event loop. The shared backend uses a seqlock (lock-free reads) plus a TTAS write spinlock.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — `@cache(max_size=N)` replaces `cachetools.func.lru_cache(maxsize=N)` or `ttl_cache` on module-level functions. Missing: `typed`, `maxsize=None`, `cache_parameters()`, `cachetools.cached(cache, key=...)`-style custom caches and keys, and LFU/RR/FIFO policies. Methods do not bind, and CacheInfo fields are named `max_size`/`current_size`.

gotchas: The latest PyPI release, 0.7.0 (2026-04-13), predates the June 2026 fixes. Those include unsound GilCell aliasing under reentrant `__eq__` (#30, critical), an out-of-bounds slab write with shared max_size=0 (#31), a data race on the lock-free read path (#37), and world-readable shm files holding pickled data (#39). Pin to master if you need them.

Shared-backend files are named from the function's `__module__` and `__qualname__` and persist across restarts. On reopen they are reused whenever version, capacity, key/value size limits and TTL match. A redeploy with changed function logic can therefore serve stale results, and closures that share a qualname share one cache. Keys or values over the size limits are silently not cached; watch `oversize_skips`.

max_size is split across up to 16 shards, each running its own SIEVE with ceil(max_size/shards) slots. Capacity is therefore approximate (max_size=100 gives 16x7=112 slots) and eviction is per shard. Also, eviction removes from a VecDeque at the hand position, which from reading the code is linear in shard size, not the O(1) the docs claim. max_size=0 still caches one entry on the memory backend (#47).

Keys follow Python equality with no `typed` option, so f(1), f(1.0) and f(True) share one entry. Keyword arguments are sorted, so f(a=1, b=2) and f(b=2, a=1) hit the same entry, unlike lru_cache. Expired TTL entries are only dropped lazily and keep their values alive until they are evicted or overwritten. Negative or NaN TTL can panic on the memory backend (#86 open).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: python-diskcache is the only other Python sibling. Pick warp_cache for in-memory memoization where per-call overhead matters, or for small primitive results shared among local workers through mmap. Pick diskcache for large or persistent values, bytes-bounded eviction, or when a crashed worker must not wedge the cache. The SIEVE and quick-cache entries are the underlying algorithm and a native Rust cache; warp_cache matters only when the caller is Python.
verified_claims_summary: These are first-party numbers from the repo's runner. The workload is 100K calls of an identity function over Zipf keys (2000 unique, ~71% hit rate at 256 entries), median of 3, on CPython 3.13.2 (Clang 20.1.0) on an unspecified Apple M-series Mac with cachetools 7.0.1. warp_cache did 20.4M calls/s against cachetools.func.lru_cache's 826K (~24.7x; 19.1-27.0x across 32-1024 entries), while stdlib functools.lru_cache did 31.0M. With 16 GIL-bound threads warp_cache did 19.5M, against 795K for cachetools with an added threading.Lock and 11.9M for lru_cache plus a Lock. cachetools.func already locks internally with a Condition, and lru_cache is documented thread-safe, so both threaded baselines pay for a lock they do not need. Plain lru_cache under threads was not measured.
status_note: Actively maintained (last master commit 2026-06-18, a batch of memory-safety and concurrency fixes), MIT-licensed and pip-installable from prebuilt wheels. The newest PyPI release (0.7.0, April 2026) lacks those fixes, and the project is small (9 stars, Beta).
